questions.q_text: Which of the following is the lowest taxonomic category in the hierarchy of classification?
questions.solution: Species is the basic and lowest taxonomic category; it is a group of individuals with fundamental similarities able to interbreed.

questions.q_text: According to NCERT, which of the following is a defining feature of all living organisms, without exception?
questions.opt_c: Ability to move from place to place
questions.opt_d: Increase in mass by surface deposition
questions.solution: All living organisms carry out the sum total of chemical reactions called metabolism; no non-living object exhibits metabolism.

questions.q_text: The system of binomial nomenclature for naming organisms was given by
questions.solution: Carolus Linnaeus provided the binomial system in which each name has two components, the generic name and the specific epithet.

questions.q_text: An actual account of the habitat and distribution of plants of a given area is provided by a
questions.solution: Flora contains the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area, while a monograph deals with one taxon in detail.

questions.q_text: A store house of collected plant specimens that are dried, pressed and preserved on sheets is called a
questions.solution: Herbarium sheets carry dried, pressed and preserved specimens along with a label giving date, place of collection and family.

questions.q_text: In a biological museum, plant and animal specimens are usually preserved in
questions.opt_d: Open glass shelves without any treatment
questions.solution: Museums maintain collections of preserved specimens kept in containers with preservative solutions; insects are preserved after killing and pinning.

questions.q_text: ICBN stands for
questions.solution: Plant names are governed by the International Code for Botanical Nomenclature, which lays down agreed rules and principles for naming.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is the correct way of writing the scientific name of mango in printed text?
questions.solution: The generic name begins with a capital letter and the specific epithet with a small letter, and the name is printed in italics.

questions.q_text: Which represents the correct sequence of taxonomic categories in descending order?
questions.opt_a: Kingdom, Division, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
questions.opt_b: Kingdom, Class, Division, Family, Order, Genus, Species
questions.opt_c: Division, Kingdom, Order, Class, Family, Species, Genus
questions.opt_d: Kingdom, Division, Order, Class, Genus, Family, Species
questions.solution: The obligate hierarchy runs Kingdom, Division (Phylum in animals), Class, Order, Family, Genus and Species, with the taxa becoming more specific downwards.

questions.q_text: Solanum, Petunia and Datura are placed together in the same
questions.solution: These three genera share vegetative and floral similarities and are grouped in the family Solanaceae.

questions.q_text: The families Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae are placed in the order
questions.solution: Both families share floral characters and are included in the order Polymoniales, an assemblage of related families.

questions.q_text: In a taxonomic key, the pair of contrasting statements used for identification is called a couplet and each individual statement is called a
questions.solution: A key is based on contrasting characters; the contrasting pair is the couplet and each statement of the couplet is a lead.

questions.q_text: Which statement about growth correctly distinguishes living from non-living things?
questions.opt_a: Only non-living objects can increase in mass
questions.opt_b: Living organisms grow only by deposition of material on the outer surface
questions.opt_c: A dead organism continues to grow from inside
questions.opt_d: Living organisms grow from inside by cell division, whereas non-living objects grow by accumulation of material on the surface
questions.solution: Intrinsic growth by cell division is characteristic of living organisms; the growth of a mountain or a sand mound is extrinsic and superficial.

questions.q_text: The number of species of living organisms that have so far been described and known is approximately
questions.solution: NCERT states that the number of species known and described ranges between 1.7 and 1.8 million, referred to as biodiversity.

questions.q_text: Assertion: Reproduction cannot be taken as an all-inclusive defining characteristic of living organisms. Reason: Mules, sterile worker bees and many infertile organisms are living but do not reproduce.
questions.opt_a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.opt_b: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.opt_c: Assertion is true but Reason is false
questions.opt_d: Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Since many living organisms do not reproduce, reproduction fails as a universal defining property, which is exactly why metabolism is preferred.

questions.q_text: Consider the statements: (i) Genus is a group of related species with more characters in common among themselves than with species of other genera. (ii) Panthera and Felis are placed in different families. (iii) Order is an assemblage of related families. (iv) Class is composed of related orders. How many statements are correct?
questions.solution: Statements (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct; Panthera and Felis are two different genera placed in the same family Felidae, so (ii) is wrong.

questions.q_text: In the name Mangifera indica, the word indica specifically represents the
questions.solution: NCERT states that the first word represents the genus while the second component denotes the specific epithet; the full binomial together denotes the species.

questions.q_text: The five kingdom system of classification was proposed by
questions.solution: R. H. Whittaker in 1969 proposed Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia using cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogeny.

questions.q_text: Which kingdom of the five kingdom system contains only prokaryotic organisms?
questions.solution: Kingdom Monera comprises bacteria, cyanobacteria, mycoplasma and archaebacteria, all of which lack a true membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.q_text: A comma-shaped bacterium is called a
questions.solution: Bacteria are grouped by shape into spherical coccus, rod-shaped bacillus, comma-shaped vibrio and spiral spirillum.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is true of Mycoplasma?
questions.opt_a: They possess a thick peptidoglycan wall
questions.opt_b: They are the largest known prokaryotes
questions.opt_d: They completely lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells
questions.solution: Mycoplasmas lack a cell wall, are the smallest living cells known, can survive without oxygen and are pathogenic in plants and animals.

questions.q_text: Viroids, causing potato spindle tuber disease, were discovered by
questions.solution: Diener discovered viroids, infectious agents smaller than viruses consisting of free RNA of low molecular weight without a protein coat.

questions.q_text: In a lichen, the algal component is known as the
questions.solution: Lichens are symbiotic associations in which the algal partner (phycobiont) is autotrophic and the fungal partner (mycobiont) absorbs water and minerals.

questions.q_text: Red tides in the sea are caused by the rapid multiplication of
questions.solution: Red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax multiply in large numbers making the sea appear red, and their toxins can kill marine animals.

questions.q_text: Methanogens are archaebacteria that
questions.opt_a: Grow in extremely salty habitats such as salt pans
questions.opt_b: Live in hot springs at very low pH
questions.opt_c: Are photosynthetic and fix atmospheric nitrogen
questions.opt_d: Are present in the gut of ruminants and produce methane from dung
questions.solution: Methanogens inhabit marshy areas and the guts of ruminant animals, where they produce methane, the chief component of biogas.

questions.q_text: Euglenoids differ from other protists in having
questions.opt_a: A protein rich pellicle instead of a cell wall
questions.opt_b: A silica shell made of two overlapping halves
questions.opt_c: A pseudoplasmodium stage in the life cycle
questions.opt_d: Cellulosic plates forming a stiff armour
questions.solution: In Euglena the cell is bounded by a flexible protein rich pellicle; stiff cellulosic plates occur in dinoflagellates and silica shells in diatoms.

questions.q_text: Which statement about slime moulds is correct?
questions.opt_a: They are photosynthetic and possess chlorophyll a and b
questions.opt_b: They are prokaryotic decomposers belonging to Monera
questions.opt_c: Their spores possess true walls and are extremely resistant, surviving for many years
questions.opt_d: They are incapable of forming any kind of aggregation
questions.solution: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists that form a plasmodium and produce fruiting bodies bearing highly resistant, long lived spores with true walls.

questions.q_text: Rhizopus and Albugo are placed in the class
questions.solution: Phycomycetes have aseptate coenocytic mycelium and produce zoospores or aplanospores; Mucor, Rhizopus and Albugo are members.

questions.q_text: The sac fungi, in which sexual spores are produced endogenously inside an ascus, include
questions.solution: Ascomycetes are called sac fungi because eight ascospores are produced inside a sac like ascus; Neurospora is widely used in biochemical and genetic work.

questions.q_text: Tobacco Mosaic Virus was crystallised, showing that viruses are largely made of proteins, by
questions.solution: Stanley crystallised TMV; Ivanowsky first recognised the agent and Beijerinck called the infectious fluid contagium vivum fluidum.

questions.q_text: Diatomaceous earth, used in polishing and in filtration of oils and syrups, is formed from the accumulated cell walls of
questions.solution: Diatom cell walls are indestructible and contain silica; their deposits laid down over billions of years form diatomaceous earth.

questions.q_text: Match the following: (i) Puccinia (ii) Ustilago (iii) Claviceps (iv) Agaricus with A. Smut B. Rust C. Mushroom D. Ergot
questions.solution: Puccinia is the rust fungus and Ustilago the smut fungus, both Basidiomycetes, Claviceps causes ergot and Agaricus is the edible mushroom.

questions.q_text: Consider the following statements about viruses: (i) A virus is a nucleoprotein and its genetic material is infectious. (ii) Most plant viruses have single stranded RNA. (iii) Bacteriophages are usually double stranded DNA viruses. (iv) Viruses possess their own metabolic machinery to generate energy. How many statements are correct?
questions.solution: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct; viruses are obligate parasites with no metabolic machinery of their own, so (iv) is wrong.

questions.q_text: Assertion: Archaebacteria are able to survive in the most harsh habitats such as extreme salt concentration and high temperature. Reason: They possess a cell wall structure that is different from that of other bacteria.
questions.opt_a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.opt_b: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.opt_c: Assertion is true but Reason is false
questions.opt_d: Assertion is false but Reason is true
questions.solution: The distinctive archaebacterial cell wall, which lacks peptidoglycan, is responsible for their survival in extreme halophilic, thermoacidophilic and methanogenic habitats.

questions.q_text: The stored food material and the main photosynthetic pigments of Chlorophyceae are respectively
questions.opt_b: Floridean starch, chlorophyll a and d
questions.solution: Green algae store food as starch and possess chlorophyll a and b, the same pigments as higher plants.

questions.q_text: Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom because
questions.opt_a: They live in soil but require water for sexual reproduction
questions.opt_b: They can live completely submerged in sea water
questions.opt_c: They possess both roots and vascular tissue
questions.opt_d: They alternate between aquatic and aerial photosynthesis
questions.solution: Bryophytes grow in damp soil but their flagellated antherozoids need a film of water to reach the archegonium.

questions.q_text: Which group is described as the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues?
questions.solution: Pteridophytes are the first land plants with xylem and phloem, and their main plant body is a sporophyte differentiated into root, stem and leaves.

questions.q_text: Gymnosperms are so named because
questions.opt_a: Their seeds are enclosed within a hard pericarp
questions.opt_b: Their ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall and the seeds remain naked
questions.opt_c: Their male gametes are always non-motile
questions.solution: In gymnosperms the ovules are borne naked on megasporophylls and after fertilisation the seeds remain uncovered by any fruit wall.

questions.q_text: Motile, multiflagellated male gametes are found in which of the following gymnosperms?
questions.solution: Among gymnosperms only Cycas and Ginkgo possess motile flagellated male gametes; in Pinus the male gametes are non-motile.

questions.q_text: In angiosperms, the primary endosperm nucleus formed by triple fusion is
questions.solution: One male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei of the central cell, so the resulting primary endosperm nucleus and the endosperm are triploid.

questions.q_text: Fucoxanthin, which imparts a characteristic brown colour, is present in members of
questions.solution: Brown algae possess chlorophyll a and c along with the xanthophyll fucoxanthin, and store food as laminarin or mannitol.

questions.q_text: A haplontic life cycle, in which the dominant plant body is a gametophyte and the zygote is the only diploid cell, is shown by
questions.solution: In Chlamydomonas, Volvox and Spirogyra the zygote undergoes meiosis at once, so no free living diploid phase exists.

questions.q_text: Which pair of pteridophytes is heterosporous, producing two kinds of spores?
questions.solution: Selaginella and Salvinia produce microspores and megaspores, and the retention of the megaspore leads to formation of the seed habit.

questions.q_text: In mosses, the first stage that develops directly from the spore is a creeping green filamentous structure called the
questions.solution: The moss life cycle has a filamentous protonema stage arising from the spore, followed by an upright leafy stage that bears the sex organs.

questions.q_text: Gemma cups containing green multicellular asexual buds are characteristic of
questions.solution: In the liverwort Marchantia, gemmae produced in gemma cups on the thallus detach and grow into new plants.

questions.q_text: Selaginella and Lycopodium are placed in which class of pteridophytes?
questions.solution: Pteridophytes are grouped as Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum).

questions.q_text: Agar, used to grow microbes and in the preparation of ice creams and jellies, is obtained from
questions.solution: Agar is a product of the red algae Gelidium and Gracilaria, whereas algin is obtained from brown algae.

questions.q_text: In Pinus, the male and female cones are
questions.opt_b: Borne on separate male and female trees always
questions.opt_c: Formed only after the tree sheds all its needles
questions.opt_d: Replaced by flowers in the second year
questions.solution: Pinus is monoecious, bearing both types of cones on the same plant, unlike Cycas in which male cones and megasporophylls occur on separate plants.

questions.q_text: Consider the statements: (i) The stored food of Rhodophyceae is floridean starch. (ii) Laminarin and mannitol are the reserve food materials of brown algae. (iii) The main plant body of a liverwort is a sporophyte. (iv) In bryophytes the sporophyte is attached to and dependent on the gametophyte. How many statements are correct?
questions.solution: Statements (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct; the dominant, free living body of a liverwort is the haploid gametophyte, so (iii) is wrong.

questions.q_text: Assertion: In gymnosperms the endosperm is haploid. Reason: The endosperm is formed by the female gametophytic tissue before fertilisation takes place.
questions.opt_a: Assertion is true but Reason is false
questions.opt_b: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.opt_c: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.opt_d: Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Gymnosperm endosperm is the haploid female gametophyte formed before fertilisation, unlike the triploid post fertilisation endosperm of angiosperms.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the members of Rhodophyceae?
questions.opt_c: Ability to grow at great depths in the sea
questions.opt_d: Storage of food as floridean starch
questions.solution: Red algae are unique in completely lacking flagella at every stage; their gametes are non-motile and are carried passively by water currents.

questions.q_text: Pneumatophores, which grow vertically upwards out of the soil to help in gaseous exchange, are found in
questions.solution: Mangrove plants such as Rhizophora growing in swampy areas produce negatively geotropic pneumatophores for respiration.

questions.q_text: Prop roots that hang from branches and provide mechanical support are characteristic of
questions.solution: The banyan tree develops thick pillar like prop roots from its horizontal branches, whereas maize and sugarcane bear stilt roots from lower nodes.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is a modified underground stem?
questions.solution: The potato tuber is an underground stem modification bearing nodes with eyes, while carrot, sweet potato and radish are storage roots.

questions.q_text: The flattened green stem of Opuntia, which performs photosynthesis, is called a
questions.solution: In Opuntia the stem is flattened and green and carries out photosynthesis, and such a modification is a phylloclade.

questions.q_text: The leaf of neem is an example of
questions.solution: In neem the leaflets are borne on a common axis, the rachis, which represents the midrib, making it pinnately compound.

questions.q_text: Whorled phyllotaxy, in which more than two leaves arise at a node, is seen in
questions.solution: Alstonia shows whorled phyllotaxy, China rose and mustard show alternate, and Calotropis shows opposite arrangement.

questions.q_text: Vexillary aestivation of the corolla is characteristic of
questions.solution: In pea and bean flowers the largest posterior standard petal overlaps the two wings, which in turn overlap the two keel petals.

questions.q_text: Free central placentation, in which ovules are borne on a central axis without septa, occurs in
questions.solution: In Dianthus and Primrose the ovary is unilocular with ovules on a central column, unlike axile placentation of tomato which has septa.

questions.q_text: Mango and coconut are examples of which fruit type?
questions.solution: Drupes develop from monocarpellary superior ovaries and possess a stony endocarp enclosing the seed.

questions.q_text: Apple is called a false fruit because
questions.opt_c: The fleshy edible part develops mainly from the thalamus
questions.opt_d: Its pericarp remains dry at maturity
questions.solution: In apple and strawberry the thalamus contributes to the fruit along with the ovary, hence they are termed false fruits.

questions.q_text: In a maize grain, the outer proteinaceous layer of the endosperm that separates it from the embryo is the
questions.solution: The endosperm of maize is bounded by a proteinous aleurone layer; the scutellum is the shield shaped cotyledon.

questions.q_text: Stamens that are attached to the petals, as in brinjal, are said to be
questions.solution: Epipetalous stamens are fused to the petals, a characteristic feature of the family Solanaceae.

questions.q_text: A flower in which the ovary is inferior and the other floral parts arise above the ovary is called
questions.solution: In epigynous flowers such as guava, cucumber and the ray florets of sunflower, the thalamus encloses the ovary and the perianth arises above it.

questions.q_text: Match the following: (i) Colocasia (ii) Ginger (iii) Onion (iv) Potato with A. Tuber B. Corm C. Bulb D. Rhizome
questions.solution: All four are underground stem modifications: Colocasia forms a corm, ginger a rhizome, onion a bulb and potato a tuber.

questions.q_text: How many of the following are stem modifications: Opuntia phylloclade, thorn of Citrus, tendril of cucumber, sweet potato, rhizome of ginger, carrot
questions.solution: Phylloclade, thorn, stem tendril and rhizome are stem modifications, while sweet potato and carrot are modified storage roots.

questions.q_text: Assertion: The corolla of Fabaceae shows vexillary aestivation. Reason: Its corolla consists of a posterior standard, two lateral wings and two anterior petals fused to form the keel.
questions.opt_a: Assertion is true but Reason is false
questions.opt_b: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.opt_c: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.opt_d: Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The papilionaceous corolla with a large overlapping standard petal is precisely what defines vexillary or papilionaceous aestivation.

questions.q_text: Which one of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
questions.solution: In Asparagus the stem is modified into cylindrical green cladodes, not tendrils; stem tendrils occur in gourds and grapevine.

questions.q_text: The increase in girth of a stem is brought about by
questions.solution: Lateral meristems such as vascular cambium and cork cambium are cylindrical meristems that add tissue radially, causing secondary growth in thickness.

questions.q_text: Collenchyma is characterised by
questions.opt_a: Uniformly lignified thick walls and dead cells
questions.opt_b: Thin walled cells with large intercellular spaces
questions.opt_c: Highly thickened walls with simple pits and no protoplasm
questions.opt_d: Deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin at the corners of the cells
questions.solution: Collenchyma cells are living, lack intercellular spaces and have corner thickenings of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin providing mechanical support to growing parts.

questions.q_text: Xylem vessels are characteristically absent in the wood of
questions.solution: Gymnosperm wood conducts water only through tracheids; vessels are an advanced feature of angiosperms.

questions.q_text: Which components of phloem are absent in gymnosperms?
questions.solution: Gymnosperm phloem possesses sieve cells and albuminous cells in place of the sieve tube elements and companion cells of angiosperms.

questions.q_text: In grasses, the guard cells surrounding the stoma are
questions.solution: Guard cells are bean shaped in dicots but dumb-bell shaped in grasses, and their inner walls are thicker than the outer walls.

questions.q_text: Casparian strips of suberin are a characteristic feature of the
questions.solution: The single layered endodermis of the root has tangential and radial walls impregnated with suberin as Casparian strips, regulating water entry into the stele.

questions.q_text: Which set of features correctly describes a typical monocotyledonous root?
questions.opt_a: Polyarch xylem, large pith and absence of secondary growth
questions.opt_b: Tetrarch xylem, no pith and normal secondary growth
questions.opt_c: Diarch xylem with a well developed cambium
questions.opt_d: Xylem and phloem present on the same radius
questions.solution: Monocot roots have more than six xylem bundles (polyarch), a large well developed pith, and they do not undergo secondary growth.

questions.q_text: The vascular bundles of a monocot stem are
questions.opt_a: Conjoint, collateral and open, arranged in a ring
questions.opt_d: Conjoint, collateral and closed, scattered in the ground tissue
questions.solution: In monocot stems the scattered bundles lack cambium (closed), are surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath and often show water containing cavities.

questions.q_text: An isobilateral leaf differs from a dorsiventral leaf in that
questions.opt_a: Its mesophyll is differentiated into palisade and spongy tissue
questions.opt_b: Its stomata occur on both surfaces and the mesophyll is not differentiated
questions.opt_d: Its epidermis is absent on the lower surface
questions.solution: In isobilateral monocot leaves both surfaces are equally exposed, stomata occur on both epidermes and the mesophyll is uniform.

questions.q_text: Spring wood or early wood is characterised by
questions.opt_a: Narrow vessels, darker colour and higher density
questions.opt_c: Wider vessels, lighter colour and lower density
questions.solution: During spring the cambium is very active and produces xylem with wider vessels; the lighter spring wood and darker autumn wood together form one annual ring.

questions.q_text: Heartwood in an old dicot stem
questions.opt_a: Is dark in colour, non-conducting and provides mechanical support
questions.opt_b: Is the peripheral lighter zone that conducts water
questions.opt_c: Consists only of living parenchyma cells
questions.opt_d: Is formed by the cork cambium
questions.solution: The central heartwood has its tracheary elements plugged with tannins, resins and gums, making it dark, durable and purely supportive.

questions.q_text: The periderm of a woody stem consists of
questions.solution: Cork cambium (phellogen) cuts off cork (phellem) to the outside and secondary cortex (phelloderm) to the inside, and the three together form the periderm.

questions.q_text: Lenticels present on the bark of woody stems function in
questions.opt_c: Exchange of gases between the internal tissues and the atmosphere
questions.opt_d: Absorption of water from the atmosphere
questions.solution: Lenticels are lens shaped openings in the periderm filled with loosely arranged complementary cells that permit gaseous exchange.

questions.q_text: Match the following: (i) Tracheids (ii) Companion cells (iii) Sclerenchyma (iv) Chlorenchyma with A. Photosynthesis B. Mechanical support C. Conduction of water D. Maintaining pressure gradient in sieve tubes
questions.solution: Tracheids conduct water, companion cells maintain the pressure gradient in sieve tubes, sclerenchyma gives mechanical support and chlorenchyma performs photosynthesis.

questions.q_text: Consider the statements: (i) The vascular cambium of a dicot stem is partly primary and partly secondary in origin. (ii) Spring wood has wider vessels and is lighter in colour than autumn wood. (iii) Heartwood is the chief water conducting tissue of an old tree. (iv) The cork cambium is also called phellogen. How many statements are correct?
questions.solution: Statements (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct; water conduction in an old trunk is carried out by the peripheral sapwood, not the heartwood.

questions.q_text: Assertion: Sapwood is lighter in colour and takes part in the conduction of water and minerals. Reason: Sapwood is the peripheral, recently formed and still functional secondary xylem of the stem.
questions.opt_a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.opt_b: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.opt_c: Assertion is true but Reason is false
questions.opt_d: Assertion is false but Reason is true
questions.solution: Sapwood consists of the outer, younger secondary xylem whose vessels are not yet blocked, which is why it remains conducting and light coloured.

questions.q_text: In a young dicotyledonous stem, the semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma lying above the phloem constitute the
questions.solution: In the dicot stem the pericycle occurs as semi-lunar sclerenchymatous patches above the phloem, whereas the hypodermis is collenchymatous and lies just below the epidermis.

questions.q_text: The idea that all cells arise from pre-existing cells, expressed as omnis cellula-e cellula, was given by
questions.solution: Virchow (1855) modified cell theory by showing that new cells are produced by division of pre-existing cells.

questions.q_text: The smallest cell known so far, measuring about 0.3 micrometre in length, is that of
questions.solution: Mycoplasma (PPLO) are the smallest living cells, about 0.3 micrometre long; bacteria and eukaryotic cells are much larger.

questions.q_text: The 70S ribosome of a prokaryotic cell is made up of two subunits of
questions.solution: The prokaryotic 70S ribosome consists of a 50S large subunit and a 30S small subunit; 80S = 60S + 40S is eukaryotic.

questions.q_text: Small circular DNA present outside the genomic DNA in many bacteria, which may confer phenotypes such as antibiotic resistance, is called
questions.solution: Plasmids are small circular extra-chromosomal DNA molecules that provide additional characters such as antibiotic resistance.

questions.q_text: The mesosome of a prokaryotic cell is formed by the infolding and extension of the
questions.solution: Mesosomes are infoldings of the plasma membrane that help in cell wall formation, DNA replication and respiration.

questions.q_text: The fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane was proposed in 1972 by
questions.solution: Singer and Nicolson (1972) gave the fluid mosaic model, in which proteins float in a fluid lipid bilayer.

questions.q_text: The middle lamella, which holds the walls of adjacent plant cells together, is chiefly made up of
questions.solution: The middle lamella is a layer of calcium pectate that cements neighbouring cells together.

questions.q_text: Chemical analysis of the human erythrocyte membrane shows that it contains approximately
questions.opt_a: 40 per cent protein and 52 per cent lipid
questions.opt_b: 20 per cent protein and 75 per cent lipid
questions.opt_c: 75 per cent protein and 20 per cent lipid
questions.opt_d: 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipid
questions.solution: NCERT gives the human RBC membrane as about 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipid.

questions.q_text: In the Golgi apparatus the convex cis face and the concave trans face are respectively known as the
questions.solution: Materials enter the Golgi at the convex cis or forming face and leave from the concave trans or maturing face.

questions.q_text: The hydrolytic enzymes packed in lysosomes are optimally active at
questions.solution: Lysosomes are rich in acid hydrolases which work best at acidic pH.

questions.q_text: In a centriole the peripheral fibrils show a cartwheel organisation and are arranged as
questions.opt_a: nine doublets with two central fibrils
questions.opt_b: nine triplets with two central fibrils
questions.opt_c: nine triplets with no central fibril
questions.opt_d: nine doublets with no central fibril
questions.solution: Each centriole has nine evenly spaced peripheral triplet fibrils and no central fibril, that is a 9 + 0 pattern.

questions.q_text: A typical nucleosome consists of a histone octamer around which is wrapped a DNA helix of about
questions.solution: A nucleosome contains about 200 bp of DNA wound around a histone octamer.

questions.q_text: Mitochondria and chloroplasts are called semi-autonomous organelles because they
questions.opt_a: are bounded by a single membrane
questions.opt_c: are budded off from the Golgi apparatus
questions.opt_d: have their own DNA and 70S ribosomes and divide by fission
questions.solution: Both organelles possess their own circular DNA, 70S ribosomes and the ability to divide independently of the cell.

questions.q_text: In bacteria a thick and tough glycocalyx is called a capsule, whereas a loose sheath of glycocalyx is called a
questions.solution: A loose sheath of glycocalyx is a slime layer, while a thick tough covering is a capsule.

questions.q_text: The most abundant polysaccharide of the plant world, forming the chief structural component of the cell wall, is
questions.solution: Cellulose, a polymer of glucose, is the main structural polysaccharide of plant cell walls and the most abundant one in plants.

questions.q_text: On the basis of the type of reaction catalysed, enzymes are grouped into how many classes?
questions.solution: Enzymes are divided into six classes: oxidoreductases, transferases, hydrolases, lyases, isomerases and ligases.

questions.q_text: Adenosine, formed by the linkage of adenine with ribose sugar, is an example of a
questions.solution: Base plus sugar is a nucleoside; addition of a phosphate group makes it a nucleotide.

questions.q_text: The bond formed between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next, with the loss of a water molecule, is a
questions.solution: A peptide bond is formed by dehydration between the carboxyl and amino groups of adjacent amino acids.

questions.q_text: The number of different kinds of amino acids that occur in proteins is
questions.solution: Only 20 types of amino acids are used to build proteins.

questions.q_text: Inulin, a storage polysaccharide of many plants, is a polymer of
questions.solution: Inulin is a polymer of fructose and is stored in roots of plants such as Dahlia.

questions.q_text: Chitin, which forms the exoskeleton of arthropods, is a polymer made up of
questions.opt_a: amino sugars such as N-acetyl glucosamine
questions.solution: Chitin is a homopolymer of N-acetyl glucosamine, an amino sugar.

questions.q_text: The most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere is
questions.solution: RuBisCO of chloroplasts is the most abundant protein in the biosphere; collagen is the most abundant in the animal world.

questions.q_text: Malonate inhibits succinic dehydrogenase because it
questions.opt_a: binds irreversibly to the metal cofactor of the enzyme
questions.opt_b: attaches to a site far away from the active site and distorts it
questions.opt_c: raises the pH of the reaction medium above the optimum
questions.opt_d: closely resembles the substrate succinate and competes for the active site
questions.solution: Malonate is a structural analogue of succinate, so it occupies the active site and acts as a competitive inhibitor.

questions.q_text: In enzymes such as peroxidase and catalase, the tightly bound haem group is an example of a
questions.solution: A prosthetic group is an organic cofactor tightly bound to the apoenzyme, as haem is in peroxidase and catalase.

questions.q_text: The acid-insoluble fraction obtained from a living tissue mainly contains
questions.opt_a: amino acids, nucleotides and simple sugars
questions.opt_c: proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides and lipids
questions.solution: Macromolecules such as proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides and lipids form the acid-insoluble fraction.

questions.q_text: The right handed helix formed by a polypeptide chain represents its
questions.solution: The helical arrangement of the polypeptide chain, the right handed alpha helix, is the secondary structure.

questions.q_text: Although lipids have molecular weights well below 800 daltons, they appear in the acid-insoluble macromolecular fraction because
questions.opt_a: they are covalently polymerised into long chains
questions.opt_b: they occur as parts of membranes which sediment as large vesicles
questions.opt_c: they are true polymers of fatty acid monomers
questions.opt_d: they dissolve completely in strong acids
questions.solution: Lipids are trapped in membrane fragments and vesicles that sediment with the macromolecular fraction.

questions.q_text: Starch gives a blue colour with iodine whereas cellulose does not, because
questions.opt_a: cellulose is a highly branched polymer
questions.opt_b: starch is built up of amino sugars
questions.opt_c: cellulose is made up of fructose units
questions.opt_d: starch forms helical secondary structures that can hold iodine molecules
questions.solution: Starch coils into a helix whose core traps iodine giving a blue colour; unbranched cellulose forms no such helix.

questions.q_text: In a typical human cell with a cell cycle of 24 hours, the M phase or cell division proper lasts for about
questions.solution: Of the 24 hour cycle, interphase occupies about 23 hours and mitosis only about one hour.

questions.q_text: Replication of DNA takes place during which phase of interphase?
questions.solution: DNA synthesis is confined to the S phase, during which DNA content doubles from 2C to 4C.

questions.q_text: The synaptonemal complex is formed between homologous chromosomes during
questions.solution: Pairing of homologues, called synapsis, occurs in zygotene and is accompanied by formation of the synaptonemal complex.

questions.q_text: Crossing over between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, mediated by recombination nodules, occurs during
questions.solution: Recombination nodules appear on the pachytene bivalents and crossing over is completed there.

questions.q_text: Terminalisation of chiasmata is completed during
questions.solution: Chiasmata formed in diplotene move towards the chromosome ends and terminalisation is completed in diakinesis.

questions.q_text: Meiosis I is described as a reductional division because
questions.opt_a: sister chromatids separate from each other
questions.opt_b: the chromosome number of each daughter cell is halved
questions.opt_c: DNA replicates once more before division
questions.solution: Homologous chromosomes separate in anaphase I, so each daughter cell gets half the chromosome number.

questions.q_text: In a plant cell with 2n = 24, the chromosomes moving to each pole at anaphase I are
questions.solution: Anaphase I separates homologues, not chromatids, so 12 chromosomes with two chromatids each move to a pole.

questions.q_text: A cell of a plant with 2n = 24 is at metaphase I of meiosis. The total number of chromatids present in it is
questions.solution: The cell still has 24 chromosomes, each with 2 chromatids, so 24 x 2 = 48 chromatids.

questions.q_text: If the DNA content of a cell in G1 phase is 2C, the DNA content of each of the two cells formed at the end of meiosis I will be
questions.solution: DNA doubles to 4C in S phase; meiosis I halves the number of chromosomes but each still has two chromatids, giving 2C per cell.

questions.q_text: A single cell undergoes five successive mitotic divisions. The number of cells finally produced is
questions.solution: The number of cells after n divisions is 2 raised to the power n, so 2^5 = 32.

questions.q_text: The minimum number of meiotic divisions required to produce 100 pollen grains is
questions.solution: Each microspore mother cell gives 4 pollen grains by one meiosis, so 100/4 = 25 meiotic divisions.

questions.q_text: The number of mitotic divisions required to produce 128 cells from a single cell is
questions.solution: Every division adds one cell, so producing 128 cells from 1 cell needs 128 - 1 = 127 divisions.

questions.q_text: Cytokinesis in a plant cell differs from that in an animal cell because
questions.opt_a: a furrow appears at the periphery and deepens inwards
questions.opt_b: a cell plate is formed which grows from the centre towards the periphery
questions.opt_c: the cell plate grows from the periphery towards the centre
questions.opt_d: no new wall material is laid down at all
questions.solution: Plant cells have a rigid wall, so a cell plate is formed in the centre and grows outward to form the middle lamella.

questions.q_text: Cells that have left the cell cycle and remain metabolically active but non-dividing are said to be in
questions.solution: In G0 cells stay metabolically active but do not proliferate unless required by the organism.

questions.q_text: The light reactions of photosynthesis take place in the
questions.solution: Photosystems and the electron transport chain are embedded in thylakoid membranes; the dark reaction occurs in the stroma.

questions.q_text: Chlorophyll a and the other photosynthetic pigments are respectively described as
questions.opt_b: protective pigment and reaction centre pigments
questions.opt_c: the chief pigment and accessory pigments
questions.solution: Chlorophyll a is the chief or reaction centre pigment; chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids are accessory pigments.

questions.q_text: Maximum photosynthesis takes place in which regions of the visible spectrum?
questions.solution: The action spectrum follows the absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a, which peaks in the blue and red regions.

questions.q_text: The first stable products of CO2 fixation in C3 and C4 plants are respectively
questions.solution: RuBisCO gives the 3 carbon PGA in C3 plants while PEP carboxylase gives the 4 carbon OAA in C4 plants.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is a C4 plant?
questions.solution: Maize, sugarcane, sorghum and Amaranthus are C4 plants; wheat, rice and potato are C3 plants.

questions.q_text: Photolysis of water during photosynthesis is associated with
questions.opt_a: photosystem I, on the outer side of the thylakoid membrane
questions.opt_c: photosystem II, on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane
questions.solution: The water splitting complex of PS II lies on the inner (lumen) side of the thylakoid membrane and releases O2, protons and electrons.

questions.q_text: Cyclic photophosphorylation differs from non-cyclic photophosphorylation in that it
questions.opt_b: synthesises only ATP and involves only PS I
questions.opt_d: involves only PS II and makes NADPH
questions.solution: In the cyclic path electrons cycle back to PS I, so only ATP is made, with no NADPH formation and no oxygen evolution.

questions.q_text: The number of turns of the Calvin cycle needed to produce one molecule of glucose is
questions.solution: One CO2 is fixed per turn, so six turns are needed to build the six carbon skeleton of glucose.

questions.q_text: For the synthesis of one molecule of glucose, the Calvin cycle of a C3 plant requires
questions.solution: Each of the six turns uses 3 ATP and 2 NADPH, giving 18 ATP and 12 NADPH per glucose.

questions.q_text: In a C4 plant, the extra ATP spent in regenerating phosphoenol pyruvate for the fixation of six molecules of CO2 is
questions.solution: Two extra ATP are used per CO2 delivered to the bundle sheath, so 6 CO2 need 12 extra ATP, raising the cost of one glucose from 18 ATP in C3 to 30 ATP in C4.

questions.q_text: Kranz anatomy of C4 leaves is characterised by
questions.opt_a: mesophyll arranged as a loose spongy tissue only
questions.opt_b: large bundle sheath cells with many chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gases and no intercellular spaces
questions.opt_c: complete absence of bundle sheath cells around the veins
questions.opt_d: bundle sheath cells that lack chloroplasts
questions.solution: The wreath of bundle sheath cells keeps CO2 concentrated around RuBisCO and prevents photorespiration.

questions.q_text: In a C4 plant, the primary CO2 acceptor and the carboxylating enzyme of the mesophyll cells are respectively
questions.solution: Mesophyll cells of C4 plants have PEP carboxylase and lack RuBisCO, which is confined to the bundle sheath.

questions.q_text: The Emerson enhancement effect demonstrated that
questions.opt_a: photosynthesis is enhanced when 680 nm and shorter wavelength light are given together, showing that two photosystems operate
questions.opt_b: photosynthesis is completely stopped in red light
questions.opt_c: only a single pigment system operates in green plants
questions.opt_d: oxygen evolution is independent of wavelength
questions.solution: The decline in yield beyond 680 nm (red drop) was reversed by supplying shorter wavelength light, revealing PS I and PS II.

questions.q_text: The law of limiting factors, which states that the rate of a process is limited by the factor nearest its minimum value, was given by
questions.solution: Blackman (1905) proposed the law of limiting factors for processes influenced by several factors.

questions.q_text: The proton gradient that drives photophosphorylation is created because
questions.opt_a: protons accumulate in the thylakoid lumen while the stroma becomes proton deficient
questions.opt_b: protons accumulate in the stroma while the lumen becomes proton deficient
questions.opt_c: protons accumulate in the intermembrane space of the chloroplast envelope
questions.opt_d: protons are pumped out of the chloroplast into the cytoplasm
questions.solution: Water splitting, electron transport and NADP reduction together build up protons in the lumen; their outward flow through the F0 channel of ATP synthase drives ATP synthesis by the F1 head.

questions.q_text: Glycolysis, also called the EMP pathway, takes place in the
questions.solution: The entire scheme of glycolysis, from glucose to pyruvic acid, occurs in the cytoplasm of the cell.

questions.q_text: The net gain of ATP by substrate level phosphorylation during glycolysis of one molecule of glucose is
questions.solution: Four ATP are formed and two are consumed in the preparatory steps, giving a net gain of two ATP.

questions.q_text: The oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA
questions.opt_a: occurs in the mitochondrial matrix and yields one NADH and one CO2 per pyruvate
questions.opt_b: occurs in the cytoplasm and yields two ATP per pyruvate
questions.opt_c: occurs on the inner mitochondrial membrane and yields FADH2
questions.opt_d: occurs in the matrix and yields one FADH2 and two CO2
questions.solution: Pyruvate dehydrogenase in the matrix removes one CO2 and reduces one NAD+ for each pyruvate oxidised.

questions.q_text: One turn of the Krebs cycle yields
questions.solution: Three dehydrogenation steps give NADH, succinate oxidation gives FADH2, succinyl CoA gives GTP and two decarboxylations release two CO2.

questions.q_text: According to the theoretical calculation given in NCERT, complete aerobic oxidation of one molecule of glucose yields
questions.solution: The calculation assumes an ordered pathway with no intermediate use, giving a net of 38 ATP per glucose.

questions.q_text: The respiratory quotient of a germinating seed that is respiring on carbohydrates is
questions.solution: Carbohydrate oxidation uses as many O2 molecules as the CO2 molecules released, so RQ = 6/6 = 1.

questions.q_text: When tripalmitin is the respiratory substrate, two molecules consume 145 molecules of O2 and release 102 molecules of CO2. The respiratory quotient is about
questions.solution: RQ = CO2 released / O2 used = 102/145 = 0.7, the typical value for fats.

questions.q_text: A respiratory quotient greater than one is obtained when the respiratory substrate is
questions.opt_a: an organic acid such as malic acid
questions.solution: Organic acids are already partly oxidised, so they release more CO2 than the O2 they consume, giving RQ above 1.

questions.q_text: In alcoholic fermentation by yeast, pyruvic acid is converted to ethanol and CO2 by the enzymes
questions.opt_d: pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase
questions.solution: Pyruvic acid decarboxylase removes CO2 to give acetaldehyde, which alcohol dehydrogenase reduces to ethanol using NADH.

questions.q_text: During fermentation, the fraction of the energy of glucose that is released is
questions.opt_d: less than seven per cent, and not all of it is trapped as ATP
questions.solution: Fermentation leaves the substrate only partly oxidised, so less than seven per cent of the energy of glucose is released.

questions.q_text: In the mitochondrial electron transport system, the mobile carrier that shuttles electrons between complex III and complex IV is
questions.solution: Cytochrome c is a small protein on the outer surface of the inner membrane that carries electrons from complex III to complex IV.

questions.q_text: Oxidation of one molecule of NADH and one molecule of FADH2 through the electron transport system yields respectively
questions.solution: NADH enters at complex I and yields 3 ATP, while FADH2 enters at complex II and yields only 2 ATP.

questions.q_text: Respiration is described as an amphibolic pathway because
questions.opt_a: it takes place only in the presence of oxygen
questions.opt_c: it is a purely catabolic sequence of reactions
questions.opt_d: respiratory intermediates take part both in breakdown and in synthesis of substrates
questions.solution: Acetyl CoA and other intermediates are withdrawn for synthesis of fatty acids and amino acids, so the pathway is both catabolic and anabolic.

questions.q_text: Substrate level phosphorylation in the Krebs cycle occurs during the conversion of
questions.solution: The only direct synthesis of GTP or ATP in the citric acid cycle occurs at the succinyl CoA to succinate step.

questions.q_text: Growth in plants is an irreversible permanent increase in size and can be measured as
questions.opt_a: rise in the temperature of the tissue
questions.opt_c: a reversible increase in cell volume
questions.opt_d: increase in cell number, fresh weight, dry weight, length or area
questions.solution: Growth is measured by many parameters such as cell number, size, fresh and dry weight, length and area.

questions.q_text: In arithmetic growth, where only one of the two daughter cells continues to divide, the length of the organ at time t is given by
questions.opt_b: Lt = L0 x e raised to rt
questions.solution: Arithmetic growth adds a constant amount per unit time, giving the linear equation Lt = L0 + rt.

questions.q_text: The sigmoid growth curve of a cell population shows the phases in the order
questions.opt_a: log phase, lag phase and stationary phase
questions.opt_b: stationary phase, lag phase and log phase
questions.opt_c: lag phase, log or exponential phase and stationary phase
questions.opt_d: lag phase, stationary phase and log phase
questions.solution: Growth is initially slow (lag), then rapid (log or exponential) and finally slows down and levels off (stationary).

questions.q_text: In the exponential growth equation W1 = W0 e raised to rt, the term r stands for
questions.opt_a: the relative growth rate, also called the efficiency index
questions.opt_b: the original size of the organ
questions.solution: r is the relative growth rate and measures the ability of the plant to produce new plant material, hence the term efficiency index.

questions.q_text: Heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur, in which juvenile leaves differ from adult leaves, is an example of
questions.solution: Plasticity is the ability of plants to form different structures in response to age or environment, as in heterophylly.

questions.q_text: Auxin was first isolated from the tips of oat coleoptiles by
questions.solution: Went recovered auxin from agar blocks placed under oat coleoptile tips; the Darwins only demonstrated phototropic bending.

questions.q_text: Bolting, the sudden elongation of internodes just before flowering in rosette plants such as beet and cabbage, is caused by
questions.solution: Gibberellins cause rapid internode elongation, producing bolting in rosette plants.

questions.q_text: Kinetin, the first cytokinin to be discovered, was obtained as a degradation product of
questions.solution: Skoog and Miller obtained kinetin from autoclaved herring sperm DNA; zeatin was later isolated from maize kernels and coconut milk.

questions.q_text: The gaseous plant growth regulator that promotes fruit ripening, horizontal growth of seedlings and swelling of the axis is
questions.solution: Ethylene is a simple gaseous PGR that hastens ripening, senescence and abscission and causes apical hook formation in dicot seedlings.

questions.q_text: Abscisic acid is called the stress hormone because it
questions.opt_a: increases tolerance to stress and brings about closure of stomata
questions.opt_b: promotes cell division at the shoot apex
questions.solution: ABA acts as a general growth inhibitor, induces dormancy and closes stomata during water stress.

questions.q_text: Removal of the shoot apex allows lateral buds to grow because it removes the source of
questions.opt_d: abscisic acid stored in the lateral buds
questions.solution: Auxin from the apical bud suppresses growth of lateral buds; decapitation removes this apical dominance.

questions.q_text: In photoperiodic induction of flowering, the site of perception of the light stimulus is the
questions.solution: Leaves perceive the photoperiod and a hormonal stimulus migrates from them to the shoot apex to induce flowering.

questions.q_text: Vernalisation is the promotion of flowering by
questions.opt_a: a period of exposure to high temperature
questions.opt_c: a period of exposure to low temperature
questions.solution: Winter varieties of wheat and biennials such as sugarbeet and cabbage flower only after a spell of low temperature.

questions.q_text: Dedifferentiation in plants is best illustrated by the
questions.opt_a: loss of protoplasm during formation of tracheary elements
questions.opt_b: growth of the pollen tube through the style
questions.opt_c: opening and closing of stomata in light and dark
questions.opt_d: formation of interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from mature parenchyma cells
questions.solution: Dedifferentiation is the regaining of the capacity to divide by cells that had already differentiated and lost it.

questions.q_text: What is the ploidy of the primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) formed after triple fusion in a typical angiosperm?
questions.solution: One haploid male gamete fuses with two haploid polar nuclei, so the PEN is triploid (n + n + n = 3n).

questions.q_text: In seeds of black pepper and beet, the persistent remnant of the nucellus is called and has a ploidy of:
questions.solution: The nucellus is sporophytic tissue of the ovule, so the residual perisperm remains diploid (2n).

questions.q_text: A typical mature angiosperm embryo sac of the Polygonum type is:
questions.solution: Three mitotic divisions of the functional megaspore give 8 nuclei; two polar nuclei share one central cell, giving 7 cells.

questions.q_text: The tough outer layer of the pollen grain, the exine, is made up of:
questions.solution: Sporopollenin is the most resistant organic material known; it is absent only at the germ pores.

questions.q_text: Emasculation in a plant-breeding programme refers to:
questions.opt_a: Removal of the stigma from a bisexual flower before pollination
questions.opt_b: Removal of anthers from a bisexual flower bud before the anthers dehisce
questions.opt_c: Covering an emasculated flower with a bag to prevent contamination
questions.opt_d: Dusting selected pollen on the stigma of a female parent
questions.solution: Emasculation prevents self-pollination in a bisexual flower; the covering step that follows is called bagging.

questions.q_text: Cleistogamous flowers are characterised by the fact that they:
questions.opt_a: Never open, are invariably autogamous and assure seed set without pollinators
questions.opt_b: Open widely and are invariably cross-pollinated by insects
questions.opt_c: Open before the anthers dehisce, thus favouring geitonogamy
questions.opt_d: Bear unisexual flowers borne on separate plants to prevent selfing
questions.solution: Anthers and stigma lie close together inside a closed flower, so pollen is shed directly on the stigma.

questions.q_text: Which wall layer of the microsporangium provides nourishment to the developing pollen grains?
questions.solution: The innermost tapetum has dense cytoplasm and often more than one nucleus, and nourishes the developing microspores.

questions.q_text: The filiform apparatus, which guides the pollen tube into the embryo sac, is a feature of the:
questions.solution: Special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip of the two synergids form the filiform apparatus.

questions.q_text: The embryo sac that develops from a single functional megaspore is described as:
questions.solution: In the Polygonum type, three of the four megaspores degenerate and only one functional megaspore forms the embryo sac.

questions.q_text: In double fertilisation, the immediate products of syngamy and of triple fusion are respectively:
questions.solution: One male gamete fuses with the egg (syngamy) forming the 2n zygote; the other fuses with two polar nuclei forming the 3n PEN.

questions.q_text: Polyembryony seen in many varieties of Citrus and Mango is chiefly due to embryos arising from:
questions.opt_a: Repeated division of the antipodal cells
questions.opt_b: Fragmentation of the free nuclear endosperm
questions.opt_c: Fusion of two synergids with a male gamete
questions.opt_d: Nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac
questions.solution: Nucellar cells protrude into the embryo sac and develop into additional embryos, an example of apomixis.

questions.q_text: How many microspore mother cells must undergo meiosis to produce 200 pollen grains?
questions.solution: Each microspore mother cell yields a tetrad of 4 pollen grains, so 200/4 = 50 cells are needed.

questions.q_text: In a flowering plant, the ploidy of an antipodal cell, the nucellus and the primary endosperm nucleus is respectively:
questions.solution: Antipodals are part of the haploid female gametophyte, nucellus is sporophytic (2n) and the PEN is triploid.

questions.q_text: What is the minimum number of meiotic divisions required to produce 100 seeds in an angiosperm, assuming one seed per ovule and one pollen grain per fertilisation?
questions.solution: 100 megaspore mother cells give 100 embryo sacs; 100 pollen grains need 25 pollen mother cells; 100 + 25 = 125 meioses.

questions.q_text: The F2 phenotypic ratio obtained by Mendel in a monohybrid cross involving complete dominance is:
questions.solution: Selfing the F1 heterozygote gives 1 homozygous dominant : 2 heterozygous : 1 recessive, i.e. 3 dominant : 1 recessive phenotype.

questions.q_text: In Antirrhinum (snapdragon), a cross between red and white flowered plants gives pink F1. The F2 phenotypic ratio is:
questions.solution: Flower colour shows incomplete dominance, so the F2 phenotypic ratio equals the genotypic ratio 1:2:1.

questions.q_text: A person with blood group AB expresses both A and B antigens. This is an example of:
questions.solution: Alleles I(A) and I(B) are equally expressed in the heterozygote, so both sugar antigens appear on the red cells.

questions.q_text: Down's syndrome in humans is caused by:
questions.solution: An extra copy of chromosome 21 (47 chromosomes) results from non-disjunction during gamete formation.

questions.q_text: Turner's syndrome in humans has the chromosomal constitution:
questions.solution: Loss of one sex chromosome gives sterile females with 45 chromosomes and rudimentary ovaries.

questions.q_text: A test cross of a dihybrid (RrYy) with a double recessive parent gives a phenotypic ratio of:
questions.solution: The dihybrid forms four gamete types in equal number and the tester contributes only recessive alleles, so all four phenotypes are equally frequent.

questions.q_text: In a dihybrid cross RrYy x RrYy, what fraction of the F2 progeny shows both recessive characters?
questions.solution: Each recessive homozygote occurs with probability 1/4, and 1/4 x 1/4 = 1/16 for both traits together.

questions.q_text: How many kinds of gametes can be produced by an individual of genotype AaBBCc?
questions.solution: Only the two heterozygous gene pairs segregate independently, giving 2 x 2 = 4 gamete types.

questions.q_text: A man of blood group AB marries a woman of blood group O. The possible blood groups of their children are:
questions.solution: The father gives I(A) or I(B) and the mother gives i, so children are I(A)i (group A) or I(B)i (group B).

questions.q_text: A carrier woman for haemophilia marries a normal man. What proportion of their sons is expected to be haemophilic?
questions.solution: Sons receive Y from the father and either the normal or the mutant X from the carrier mother, so half are affected.

questions.q_text: Phenylketonuria, in which a single gene mutation affects several apparently unrelated traits, illustrates:
questions.solution: The defective enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase causes mental retardation plus reduced hair and skin pigmentation.

questions.q_text: In a pedigree, a trait appears in both sexes with equal frequency and two unaffected parents have an affected daughter. The trait is most probably:
questions.solution: Unaffected parents producing an affected child means both are heterozygous carriers, and equal sex frequency rules out X-linkage.

questions.q_text: A cross RrYy x RrYy produced 1600 seeds. How many of these are expected to be homozygous for both dominant genes (RRYY)?
questions.solution: RRYY occurs in 1/16 of the F2, and 1600 x 1/16 = 100 seeds.

questions.q_text: A test cross AaBb x aabb gave 41 AaBb, 43 aabb, 8 Aabb and 8 aaBb. This result indicates that the two genes are:
questions.opt_b: Linked, with about 16 per cent recombination
questions.opt_c: Linked, with about 50 per cent recombination
questions.solution: Parental types greatly exceed recombinants; recombination frequency = (8+8)/100 = 16 per cent, showing linkage.

questions.q_text: Hershey and Chase labelled bacteriophages with radioactive isotopes to prove DNA is the genetic material. The isotopes used were:
questions.solution: DNA contains phosphorus but no sulphur, while protein contains sulphur but no phosphorus, allowing the two to be traced separately.

questions.q_text: The gaps between the discontinuously synthesised Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand are sealed by:
questions.solution: DNA ligase joins the free 3' OH end of one fragment to the 5' phosphate of the next, forming a phosphodiester bond.

questions.q_text: Which of the following triplets is NOT a termination (stop) codon?
questions.solution: AUG is the initiation codon and also codes for methionine; UAA, UAG and UGA are the three stop codons.

questions.q_text: Meselson and Stahl grew Escherichia coli in a medium containing 15NH4Cl to demonstrate:
questions.opt_c: The genetic code is a triplet code
questions.solution: After one generation in 14N medium all DNA was of hybrid density, which is expected only if each daughter DNA keeps one parental strand.

questions.q_text: In the transcription unit of a bacterium, the enzyme that catalyses the polymerisation of ribonucleotides in the 5' to 3' direction is:
questions.solution: A single DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, with sigma and rho factors, carries out initiation, elongation and termination in bacteria.

questions.q_text: If a double-stranded DNA molecule contains 20 per cent adenine, the percentage of guanine in it will be:
questions.solution: A = T = 20 per cent, so A + T = 40 per cent; the remaining 60 per cent is shared equally by G and C, giving G = 30 per cent.

questions.q_text: The length of a DNA double helix containing 3 x 10^5 base pairs, taking 0.34 nm as the distance between adjacent base pairs, is about:
questions.solution: Length = number of bp x 0.34 nm = 3 x 10^5 x 0.34 = 1.02 x 10^5 nm (about 0.102 mm).

questions.q_text: A typical nucleosome consists of a histone octamer wrapped by DNA of approximately:
questions.solution: Negatively charged DNA winds around the positively charged histone octamer; a nucleosome contains about 200 bp of DNA helix.

questions.q_text: In the lac operon of E. coli, the product of the i gene:
questions.opt_b: Acts as an inducer of the operon
questions.opt_c: Is a repressor protein that binds the operator region
questions.opt_d: Is a permease that transports lactose
questions.solution: The i gene codes for the repressor, which blocks transcription until the inducer lactose binds and inactivates it.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is NOT a post-transcriptional modification of hnRNA in eukaryotes?
questions.opt_a: Capping with methyl guanosine triphosphate at the 5' end
questions.opt_b: Tailing with adenylate residues at the 3' end
questions.opt_d: Addition of a sigma factor at the 5' end
questions.solution: Sigma factor is a bacterial transcription initiation factor; capping, tailing and splicing convert hnRNA into mature mRNA.

questions.q_text: DNA fingerprinting depends mainly on polymorphism in:
questions.opt_c: The promoter of the beta-globin gene
questions.opt_d: Repetitive satellite DNA showing variable number of tandem repeats
questions.solution: VNTR satellite DNA shows high degree of polymorphism, so the band pattern differs between individuals except identical twins.

questions.q_text: A double-stranded DNA segment contains 1000 nucleotides in all, of which 200 are adenine. The number of cytosine residues present is:
questions.solution: A = T = 200, so A + T = 400; the remaining 600 nucleotides are G and C in equal number, giving C = 300.

questions.q_text: The total length of DNA in a human diploid cell (6.6 x 10^9 base pairs) is approximately:
questions.solution: 6.6 x 10^9 bp x 0.34 x 10^-9 m per bp gives about 2.2 m of DNA packed into the nucleus.

questions.q_text: The coding sequence of an mRNA is 1200 nucleotides long and includes the termination codon. The polypeptide translated from it will contain:
questions.solution: 1200/3 = 400 codons, but the stop codon does not code for an amino acid, so 399 amino acids are incorporated.

questions.q_text: The intrinsic rate of natural increase (r) of a population is given by:
questions.opt_d: Birth rate divided by death rate
questions.solution: r combines the per capita birth and death rates and is the single most important parameter assessing population growth.

questions.q_text: The exponential growth equation dN/dt = rN describes a population that:
questions.opt_a: Grows with limited resources and gives a sigmoid curve
questions.opt_b: Grows without any resource limitation and gives a J-shaped curve
questions.opt_c: Has reached the carrying capacity of the habitat
questions.opt_d: Is declining because the death rate exceeds the birth rate
questions.solution: Exponential or geometric growth occurs when food and space are unlimited, producing a J-shaped curve on arithmetic plotting.

questions.q_text: A lichen, in which a fungus and a photosynthetic alga live together to the benefit of both, is an example of:
questions.solution: Mutualism is a (+ +) interaction in which both interacting species gain benefit.

questions.q_text: Aestivation in some snails and fish is best described as:
questions.opt_a: A state of winter sleep that avoids cold
questions.opt_b: Seasonal migration to a more hospitable area
questions.opt_c: A state of summer dormancy that avoids heat and desiccation
questions.opt_d: A suspended stage of development in the life cycle of zooplankton
questions.solution: Aestivation is summer dormancy; hibernation is winter sleep and diapause is suspended development.

questions.q_text: According to Allen's Rule, mammals of colder climates generally have:
questions.opt_a: Longer ears and limbs to maximise heat loss
questions.opt_b: Shorter ears and limbs to minimise heat loss
questions.opt_c: A thinner layer of subcutaneous fat
questions.opt_d: A higher surface area to volume ratio
questions.solution: Reducing the length of extremities lowers the surface area available for radiating body heat.

questions.q_text: In the logistic growth equation dN/dt = rN (K - N)/K, the symbol K stands for:
questions.opt_d: Number of individuals added per unit time
questions.solution: K is the maximum population size the habitat can support with its available resources.

questions.q_text: Gause's competitive exclusion principle states that:
questions.opt_a: Competing species always evolve to use identical resources
questions.opt_b: The superior competitor is always eliminated from the habitat
questions.opt_c: Two closely related species competing for the same limiting resource cannot coexist indefinitely
questions.opt_d: Competition occurs only between individuals of the same species
questions.solution: The inferior competitor is eventually eliminated unless the species diverge in resource use (resource partitioning).

questions.q_text: An orchid growing as an epiphyte on a mango branch represents an interaction that is:
questions.opt_a: Beneficial to both the orchid and the mango tree
questions.opt_b: Beneficial to the orchid and neutral for the mango tree
questions.opt_c: Harmful to the mango tree and beneficial to the orchid
questions.opt_d: Harmful to the orchid and neutral for the mango tree
questions.solution: Commensalism is a (+ 0) interaction in which one partner benefits while the other is neither harmed nor helped.

questions.q_text: The Mediterranean orchid Ophrys attracts its bee pollinator by:
questions.opt_a: Having a petal that mimics the female bee, inducing pseudocopulation
questions.opt_b: Secreting large amounts of nectar rich in sugars
questions.opt_c: Releasing a foul smell that mimics rotting flesh
questions.opt_d: Producing sticky pollinia that adhere to passing wind currents
questions.solution: Sexual deceit: the male bee attempts to copulate with the flower and transfers pollen between flowers.

questions.q_text: An age pyramid with a broad base and a narrow apex indicates a population that is:
questions.opt_a: Stable, with equal numbers in all age classes
questions.opt_c: Composed almost entirely of post-reproductive individuals
questions.opt_d: Growing rapidly, with a large proportion of pre-reproductive individuals
questions.solution: A wide base means many young individuals who will enter the reproductive phase, so the population expands.

questions.q_text: In a population of 5000 mice, 200 individuals were born and 100 died in one year. The intrinsic rate of natural increase (r) is:
questions.solution: b = 200/5000 = 0.04 and d = 100/5000 = 0.02, so r = b - d = 0.02 per individual per year.

questions.q_text: A survivorship curve in which mortality is extremely heavy in the early stages of life, as in oysters, is:
questions.opt_a: Type III, a sharply falling convex-downward curve
questions.opt_b: Type I, a curve that stays high and drops only in old age
questions.opt_c: Type II, a straight diagonal line
questions.solution: Type III organisms produce enormous numbers of young of which very few survive the juvenile stage.

questions.q_text: Which statement about the logistic model of population growth is INCORRECT?
questions.opt_a: The growth curve is sigmoid and has a lag phase, an acceleration phase and a plateau
questions.opt_b: When N is very small compared with K, growth is nearly exponential
questions.opt_c: The rate of increase dN/dt is maximum when the population size N equals the carrying capacity K
questions.opt_d: The model is considered more realistic than exponential growth because resources are finite
questions.solution: When N = K the term (K - N)/K becomes zero, so dN/dt is zero, not maximum; growth is fastest near N = K/2.

questions.q_text: Net primary productivity (NPP) of an ecosystem is obtained as:
questions.opt_a: Gross primary productivity plus respiratory losses of producers
questions.opt_c: Gross primary productivity minus respiratory losses of producers
questions.opt_d: The total biomass present at a given time
questions.solution: NPP = GPP - R; it is the biomass actually available to heterotrophs of the next trophic level.

questions.q_text: Which ecological pyramid is always upright in any ecosystem?
questions.solution: Energy is lost as heat at every transfer, so a higher trophic level can never contain more energy than the level below.

questions.q_text: A detritus food chain begins with:
questions.solution: The detritus food chain starts from dead plant and animal remains and is run by decomposers such as fungi and bacteria.

questions.q_text: The breakdown of detritus into smaller particles by detritivores such as earthworms is called:
questions.solution: Fragmentation is the first step of decomposition and greatly increases the surface area for microbial action.

questions.q_text: The amount of living material present in a trophic level at a given time is termed:
questions.solution: Standing crop is measured as biomass or number per unit area; standing state refers to the amount of nutrients in the soil.

questions.q_text: The dark coloured, amorphous, highly resistant substance formed in the soil during decomposition is:
questions.solution: Humification produces humus, which undergoes very slow microbial degradation and acts as a nutrient reservoir.

questions.q_text: An inverted pyramid of biomass is characteristically seen in:
questions.opt_a: A sea or pond ecosystem, where phytoplankton biomass is less than that of zooplankton and fishes
questions.opt_d: Any ecosystem when energy is measured instead of biomass
questions.solution: Small, fast-reproducing phytoplankton support a much larger standing biomass of consumers at any one time.

questions.q_text: The pyramid of numbers is inverted in:
questions.opt_a: A grassland with grass, insects and birds
questions.opt_b: A single big tree supporting numerous insects and their parasitic birds
questions.opt_c: A pond with algae, zooplankton and fish
questions.opt_d: A crop field with plants, herbivores and carnivores
questions.solution: One producer supports many herbivores, which in turn support still more parasites, so the pyramid widens upwards.

questions.q_text: The ten per cent law of energy transfer between trophic levels was given by:
questions.solution: Lindeman stated that only about 10 per cent of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next.

questions.q_text: The pioneer species in a typical xerarch succession on a bare rock are:
questions.solution: Lichens secrete acids that weather the rock and build up soil, later replaced by bryophytes and higher plants.

questions.q_text: Which of the following nutrient cycles is sedimentary and lacks a significant gaseous phase?
questions.solution: The main reservoir of phosphorus is rock, and atmospheric inputs of phosphorus are negligible.

questions.q_text: If the producers of a grassland fix 10,000 J of energy, the energy available at the third trophic level according to the ten per cent law is:
questions.solution: 10,000 J at producers gives 1000 J to herbivores (second level) and 100 J to primary carnivores (third level).

questions.q_text: The gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is 25 kcal/m2/day and 60 per cent of it is used up in respiration by the producers. The net primary productivity is:
questions.solution: Respiration uses 0.6 x 25 = 15 kcal, so NPP = 25 - 15 = 10 kcal/m2/day.

questions.q_text: According to IUCN (2004), the number of plant and animal species described so far is slightly more than:
questions.solution: Robert May's statistical analysis places the probable global total nearer 7 million, so most species are still undescribed.

questions.q_text: The rivet popper hypothesis, which compares species in an ecosystem with rivets in an aeroplane, was proposed by:
questions.solution: Ehrlich used the analogy to argue that loss of each species weakens the ecosystem, key species being like rivets on the wings.

questions.q_text: Which of the following is an example of in situ conservation?
questions.solution: In situ conservation protects the threatened species in its natural habitat; the other options are ex situ methods.

questions.q_text: Cryopreservation of gametes at minus 196 degrees Celsius and maintenance of seed banks are examples of:
questions.solution: Ex situ conservation removes the threatened organism or its propagules from the habitat and maintains them under special care.

questions.q_text: The three biodiversity hot spots that lie wholly or partly in India are:
questions.opt_a: Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Himalaya, and Indo-Burma
questions.opt_b: Western Ghats, Sundarbans and Thar desert
questions.opt_c: Himalaya, Gangetic plains and Andaman islands
questions.opt_d: Indo-Burma, Deccan plateau and Eastern Ghats
questions.solution: These are among the 34 global hot spots, which are areas of very high endemism facing severe habitat loss.

questions.q_text: In Ehrlich's 'evil quartet' of causes of biodiversity loss, the single most important cause is:
questions.solution: Destruction and fragmentation of habitats, as in tropical rainforests, is listed as the leading driver of extinctions.

questions.q_text: The introduction of the Nile perch into Lake Victoria in Africa led to:
questions.opt_a: Extinction of more than 200 species of native cichlid fishes
questions.opt_b: A large increase in the diversity of native cichlids
questions.opt_c: Eutrophication of the lake by nitrogen fixation
questions.opt_d: Extinction of the water hyacinth from the lake
questions.solution: Invasive alien species can drive native species to extinction by predation and competition.

questions.q_text: Species diversity generally shows a latitudinal gradient because:
questions.opt_a: Tropical regions have remained relatively undisturbed for long periods and have constant environments
questions.opt_b: Temperate regions receive more solar energy throughout the year
questions.opt_c: Polar regions have had the longest evolutionary time without glaciation
questions.opt_d: Tropical soils are poorer in nutrients, favouring speciation
questions.solution: Long evolutionary time, constant environment and greater solar energy all favour high tropical species richness.

questions.q_text: India, with about 2.4 per cent of the world's land area, harbours what share of the global species diversity?
questions.solution: This disproportionately high share makes India one of the world's mega-diverse countries.

questions.q_text: In the species-area relationship log S = log C + Z log A, the value of the slope Z for species-area relationships analysed within a small region is usually:
questions.solution: Z lies in the narrow range 0.1 to 0.2 regardless of taxonomic group or region; it becomes 0.6 to 1.2 for very large areas such as continents.

questions.q_text: For a group of organisms, the species-area relation is S = C x A^Z with C = 10 and Z = 0.5. The number of species expected in an area of 100 units is:
Sacred groves, which are among the finest examples of community-based in situ conservation in India, are found in:
questions.opt_a: Sundarbans of West Bengal and Rann of Kutch
questions.opt_b: Nilgiri biosphere reserve and Corbett national park only
questions.opt_c: Only in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
questions.opt_d: Khasi and Jaintia hills of Meghalaya and Aravalli hills of Rajasthan
questions.solution: Sacred groves are tracts of forest given total protection on religious grounds, also seen in the Western Ghats and Bastar region.
